{"path":"snake_zai-glm-5.3_01.html","edit_description":"Create a NEW single-file HTML5 Snake game (HTML + CSS + JavaScript all inlined, no external dependencies, no frameworks). File: snake_zai-glm-5.3_01.html. This is a full-file generation from scratch — produce a complete, polished, working game.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Classic Snake on a 30x30 grid rendered with <canvas> (e.g. 600x600 px, 20px cells). Wrap the canvas in a styled container with a HUD above it.
2. TWO snakes compete (Player 1 and Player 2). Each snake: array of grid cells (head first), direction, color, score, alive flag, controls type (human/cpu).
3. THREE game modes selectable from the start menu (press 1, 2 or 3, or click buttons):
   - MODE 1 "Human vs Human": Snake 1 controlled with WASD, Snake 2 with Arrow keys.
   - MODE 2 "CPU vs Human": Snake 1 is CPU-controlled (auto food search), Snake 2 is human with Arrow keys.
   - MODE 3 "CPU vs CPU": both snakes CPU-controlled (spectator mode).
4. Continuous movement: game ticks on a fixed interval (e.g. 110ms via setInterval or requestAnimationFrame accumulator). Each tick both snakes move one cell in their current direction. Direction changes are queued (input buffer) and cannot reverse 180° (e.g. moving right can't switch directly to left).
5. Food: single food item spawned at a random free cell. When a snake head reaches food: score +1, snake grows (don't remove tail this tick), new food spawns. Draw the food distinctly (e.g. red/pink pulsing circle or apple with glow).
6. Collisions end the game: snake head hits a wall (grid border), its own body, or the other snake's body. If both snakes die in the same tick it's a DRAW. If exactly one dies, the survivor wins; in single-snake-death case game over screen shows the winner and both scores. Head-on head collision (both heads same cell) = both die = draw. Head-to-head swap (snakes pass through each other swapping cells) also kills both.
7. CPU AI (food search): each tick the CPU snake runs BFS pathfinding from its head to the food, treating walls and BOTH snakes' bodies as obstacles (use each snake's current occupied cells; optionally treat cells that will free up — tail cells — as walkable for smarter play). Take the first step of the shortest path. If NO path exists, fall back to a survival heuristic: among the 3 non-reversing directions choose a safe one (not wall/body), preferring the direction whose resulting region has the largest free space (flood fill count); if no safe move exists, keep current direction (dies). Update AI decision every tick before movement. Cap BFS/flood-fill work reasonably (grid is only 900 cells, fine).
8. Score display DURING gameplay: HUD above the canvas showing both snakes' names/colors/scores live (e.g. "P1 (WASD): 7  |  Mode: Human vs Human  |  P2 (Arrows): 4"), plus a "Speed" or tick indicator optional. HUD updates immediately on eat.
9. Start menu screen: overlay div centered over/above the board with title "SNAKE", the three mode options listed with their key hints and control schemes, and instructions. Keyboard 1/2/3 starts the chosen mode; clicking the buttons also works.
10. Game over screen: overlay showing "GAME OVER", the result (winner snake with its color, or DRAW), final scores for both snakes, and "Press R or ENTER to restart". Any of R / Enter / Space restarts: R and Enter return to the START MENU; alternatively provide "R = play again same mode" and "M or Esc = menu". Implement: R/Enter = replay same mode immediately, M/Esc = back to menu. State this on screen.
11. Restart with keypress must work (as specified above). Also allow pausing with P/Space during play (nice-to-have, show "PAUSED" overlay).
12. Visual polish: dark theme background (deep gradient), canvas board with subtle grid checkerboard, rounded snake segments with gradient colors (Snake 1 = green/teal, Snake 2 = blue/purple or cyan), distinct snake heads (eyes based on direction), glowing food, rounded corners, drop shadows, Google-font-free (use system font stack or monospace for retro feel). Add a subtle CSS animation (title glow / pulsing food). Overlays styled with translucent dark backdrop, blur backdrop-filter, clear typography.
13. Code quality: clean, organized JavaScript in an IIFE or plain script — constants at top (GRID=30, CELL=20, TICK_MS, colors), a game state object, functions: init/reset, spawnFood, tick/update, moveSnake, checkCollisions, aiChooseDirection (BFS + fallback flood fill), render/draw, HUD update, screen switching. Use addEventListener('keydown'). preventDefault on arrow keys/space so the page doesn't scroll. Ensure snake input queues process one turn per tick to avoid double-turn self-collision in one tick.
14. Snakes start positions: Snake 1 at left area facing right (e.g. row 7, x 5..7), Snake 2 at right area facing left (mirrored, e.g. row 22, x 24..22). Length 3 each. Initial scores 0.

Make sure the game is fully playable, has no bugs (double-turn bug, reversing bug, food spawning on snakes, etc.), and all listed features work. Single file, everything inlined."}
